key_insight: ST2M uses crystal symmetry to guide generation, jointly modeling discrete and continuous variables to produce stable, novel crystal candidates under prescribed Wyckoff patterns.
engineering_relevance: Symmetry-constrained generation could focus materials screening on chemically viable candidates while respecting required crystallographic constraints.
method: Represent crystals as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits.
Apply symmetry-guided discrete–continuous diffusion with degree-of-freedom masks.
Use a twin-branch Transformer to jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 96.37% structural validity; for known patterns, 23.86% of generated structures met stability, uniqueness, and novelty criteria, a 68.15% relative improvement over the best baseline; first-principles calculations identified 21 previously unreported stable structures among selected low-predicted-energy candidates.
watch_item: First-principles validation covered selected candidates, so the 21 discoveries do not establish the stability rate across all generated structures.
paper_title: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
